Anthropic is now offering US K-12 teachers free access to premium features of its Claude AI. The move is part of a new "Claude for Teachers" programme.

"Claude for Teachers" gives US educators free access to Anthropic's paid AI features.

Anthropic on Tuesday announced a new "Claude for Teachers" initiative, featuring a suite of Claude skills built specifically for education.

"Once verified, K-12 educators in the United States will have access to Claude for Teachers, including the Learning Commons connector, and a tailored set of teaching skills designed in line with the learning sciences," Anthropic said.

"These skills, developed alongside Learning Commons, are built around the tasks teachers say matter most. We evaluated them for rigour, pedagogical alignment, and classroom practicality, and refined them based on early input from frontline educators, including teachers at schools like Prospect Schools in Brooklyn," Anthropic said.

"Claude for Teachers" includes access to Claude Cowork and Claude Code, giving educators a way to tap into Anthropic's newest AI technology. The company also recently published a guide on AI's applications in teaching for educators interested in bringing AI into the classroom.

Anthropic said the new "Claude for Teachers" programme is designed for individual educators. At the same time, the AI company said it is also working on "dedicated options for schools and districts".

The rollout includes a one-year free licence to Claude's premium tier. Eligible teachers have until 30 June 2027 to apply and take advantage of the offer.

For more on Anthropic's new "Claude for Teachers" programme, click here. OpenAI also rolled out "ChatGPT for Teachers" in November last year, which remains available to eligible educators.
